name: Global food prices
summary: FAO food price index 133.9 in October, below the 135 Alert line but up 5.9% on a year; India weighs rice export curbs
state: The FAO Food Price Index averaged 133.9 points in October, down 1.2% on September but 5.9% above a year earlier (FAO via Bizcommunity, 6 Nov). The annual rise meets the Watch line while the index stays below 135. India's government is weighing a 30% duty or a minimum export price on non-basmati rice, reported on 22–23 Nov, but no curb had been imposed (InfoArroz). The next FAO release is due on 4 Dec.
for_you: UK food prices tend to follow global commodity costs with a lag of several months. The ONS publishes monthly food inflation figures.
rubric_hit: Watch: FAO index +5.9% y/y > +5% line; 133.9 < 135 Alert line; no multi-exporter staple bans

sources.title: Bizcommunity — Global food prices fall in October as sugar rises for fourth month
InfoArroz — India: Govt mulls curbs on rice exports

why: Food prices drive inflation, hunger and political unrest; poorer countries spend up to half of income on food.
drivers: Harvests, weather, fertiliser and energy costs, export bans, conflict in breadbaskets.

rubric.alert: FFPI > 135, or multiple major exporters ban exports of a staple.
rubric.watch: FFPI 120–135, or y/y > +5%, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: FAO Food Price Index < 120 and y/y change < +5%.
